pages.text: Kota lined the hall with a wooden boat, basin, and dipper. "Sea here, harbor there!" Toys filled the corridor.
A bull arrived carrying a huge load. "Oh, nowhere to walk." With his baggage, he tilted this way and that.
"Could you move a little? My load is heavy." Kota pouted. "But this is my sea..."
Dad crouched beside Kota. "Shall we make a path? Send the boats into harbor." Kota's eyes shone. "Harbor?"
Kota carried the wooden boat into the basket at the hall's end. "One ship arriving!" A handspan of floor opened.
The basin and dipper went into harbor in turn. The path widened. "Move Aside—A Path!" Kota spread both arms.
The bull strode through with his load. "Thank you, harbor captain! You made it easy." Kota's tail shot up.
He took a handful of chestnuts from his load and put them in Kota's hand. "Payment for your path." Kota's eyes grew round as chestnuts.
At sunset, Kota carried the boat to the basket, counting aloud. "One, pick up! Two, into harbor! Three, path wide open!" The hall stayed clear.
That evening, Dad held Kota's hand as they walked down the clean hall. "Everyone walks easily on your path." Kota pointed ahead and smiled. "Tomorrow, Move Aside—A Path!"
